title: Make combined Docs navigation responsive and accessible
description:
## Why
The combined Docs stream loses navigation on narrow screens, overflows 320px, exposes active state only visually, ignores reduced motion, and flattens chapter/subsection headings.

## Evidence
- `src/styles/docs.css:284-291` hides the rail below 920px without a compact alternative.
- At 320px the document is about 393px wide, `.docs-stream` about 377px; wide tables spill and the nav overlaps the H1.
- `src/pages/docs/index.astro:125-146` has no `aria-current`.
- `src/styles/docs.css:3-5` retains smooth scrolling with reduced motion.
- Chapter and subsection headings are both H2 in the combined document.

## Scope
In: one-source compact/desktop navigation; eliminate 320px overflow/overlap; programmatic current state; reduced motion; meaningful one-H1 chapter/subsection hierarchy.
Out: replacing Starlight, standalone redesign, combined search, content rewrite, or the prerequisite anchor-emission repair.

## Implementation Notes
Reuse current rail data and native HTML/CSS. Do not duplicate navigation truth between breakpoints.

## Verification
No overflow at 320/412/desktop; every chapter keyboard/touch reachable; current state exposed; reduced motion is non-smooth; outline nests correctly; Axe/check/build/built-site browser pass.

## Stop Conditions
Stop if the design duplicates anchor/navigation data. Do not hide readable content to suppress overflow.

## Maintenance Notes
Effort: M. Risk: MED. Impact: HIGH. Confidence: HIGH.
acceptance_criteria:
[ ] Narrow and desktop navigation use one source of truth.
[ ] No overflow or header overlap at 320px and 412px.
[ ] Active state, reduced motion, keyboard/touch access, and heading hierarchy are accessible.
[ ] Axe, check, build, and built-site proof pass.
notes: Implemented one-source responsive Docs navigation with the existing rail: desktop retains chapter/subsection navigation; 920px and below exposes the same chapter links as a sticky horizontal scroller. Active state is programmatic via aria-current, with rail-local scrolling that does not cancel fragment navigation. Combined output now has one H1, eight chapter H2s, and document subsections shifted to H3/H4 while standalone pages remain unchanged. Narrow layouts add header clearance, wrap long inline code, contain wide tables/code, and expose scrollable regions to keyboard users. Reduced motion disables smooth scrolling. The custom dark page declares its theme so Expressive Code uses its accessible dark palette. Added @axe-core/playwright and built-browser coverage for 320/412/desktop overflow, header separation, all eight chapter links by keyboard and click, active state, reduced motion, heading structure, and zero Axe violations. Visual inspection passed at 1440x900, 412x915, and 320x568. Verification on 2026-08-12: bun install --frozen-lockfile passed; bun run check reported zero diagnostics; bun run test:e2e rebuilt 13 static pages and passed 21/21; git diff --check passed; no preview server remained.
close_reason: Combined Docs now has one-source responsive navigation, no 320/412 overflow or header overlap, programmatic current state, reduced-motion behavior, semantic heading hierarchy, and clean built-site accessibility proof.

title: Exercise the built static site in browser verification
description:
## Why
The browser suite runs against Astro development, so it does not prove the static artifact published by Vercel. Pagefind, pre-script HTML, static 404/routing, and artifact assets can regress while all browser tests pass.

## Evidence
- `playwright.config.ts:4-9` starts `bun run dev`.
- Pagefind is produced only by the production build path.
- All 32 browser tests pass even though built combined Docs HTML has broken pre-script IDs.
- `bun run build` emits 13 pages and Pagefind; no repeatable local browser command exercises that output.

## Scope
In: make the release-facing browser command build/serve generated output; cover Pagefind, static assets, pre-script HTML, canonical routing/404, and strongest journeys; keep one browser/project.
Out: hosted CI, matrices, visual snapshots, another framework, monitoring, or full Vercel emulation. A separate fast dev command survives only with material value.

## Implementation Notes
Use the existing build, Playwright, and the smallest available static-serving path. Generated output owns release proof.

## Verification
From clean output, one command builds/tests only static output; no fallback to `src`/dev; Pagefind returns a known Docs result; static 404/assets and pre-JS assertions run; check/build/new browser command pass.

## Stop Conditions
Stop before adding hosted CI or a server dependency without a separate decision. Avoid duplicate dev/built suites with the same contract.

## Maintenance Notes
Effort: M. Risk: MED. Release impact: HIGH. Confidence: HIGH.
acceptance_criteria:
[ ] Release browser command builds and serves only static output.
[ ] Pagefind, static 404/assets, pre-script HTML, and representative journeys are covered.
[ ] No silent Astro-dev fallback exists.
[ ] No browser matrix, hosted CI, or redundant framework is added.
[ ] Check/build/built browser suite pass from clean output.
notes: Accepted state after fresh-eyes and simplification: Playwright builds the site, serves only dist through Astro preview, refuses to reuse an existing server, and runs one Chromium project. The artifact test proves the workspace image and uses the real Starlight search dialog from Start to find Configure; the prior direct Pagefind module import and custom type shim were deleted. Generated 404 title proof reuses the existing removed-Blog-route loop instead of adding another navigation. The JavaScript-disabled Docs test exercises built HTML. Rejected further deletion of explicit server non-reuse or the named Chromium device because those lines make the release contract and browser context clear. Evidence on 2026-08-12: bun run check passed with zero diagnostics; bun run build emitted 13 pages and Pagefind; bun run test:e2e rebuilt dist and passed all 18 tests; git diff --check passed; Astro reported no preview server after the suite.
close_reason: Fresh-eyes corrections now verify Pagefind through the user-facing Starlight UI and reuse the existing generated-404 journey with less test code; full built-artifact verification remains green.

title: Publish the Yazelix family root and Eon site when ready
description:
## Why
Yazelix is the established product family. Yazelix Nova and Yazelix Eon are parallel product lines with similar user-facing goals and different architectures. When Eon has an accepted public site, the apex can present that family without moving Nova or making either line appear deprecated.

## Accepted Decision
- Public product names are **Yazelix Nova** and **Yazelix Eon**.
- Eon came after Nova chronologically; that does not make it a replacement or make Nova legacy.
- Both lines are intended to evolve in parallel.
- The already-owned `yazelix.com` domain is sufficient; no additional registered domain is required.
- **Yazelix Nova launches and remains canonical at `https://nova.yazelix.com`.**
- There is no Nova-at-root phase, later Nova move, or established apex URL set that must be redirected to Nova.
- After Yazelix Eon has an accepted public site and the user activates this issue:
  - `https://yazelix.com` becomes a concise Yazelix family landing page;
  - `https://eon.yazelix.com` becomes the canonical Yazelix Eon site;
  - `https://nova.yazelix.com` continues unchanged as the canonical Yazelix Nova site.
- Any separately purchased Yazelix Nova or Yazelix Eon domain is defensive/redirect-only unless a later explicit decision changes this contract.

## Scope
In:
- Trigger only after the Nova launch is complete and Yazelix Eon has an accepted public website.
- Publish a small family chooser that explains the shared Yazelix promise and the two architectural lines without ranking one as the replacement.
- Connect the independently owned Eon site at `eon.yazelix.com`.
- Configure DNS, TLS, sitemap/canonical metadata, and cross-links for the apex and Eon hosts.
- Verify that the existing Nova host, paths, canonical metadata, documentation truth, release evidence, and deployment owner remain unchanged.
- Verify that each product keeps its own documentation, release truth, and deployment owner while sharing the Yazelix brand.

Out:
- Building Yazelix Eon, writing its documentation, merging the two site codebases, or creating shared runtime/release policy.
- Buying a second domain as a prerequisite.
- Moving Nova, changing Nova canonical URLs, creating apex-to-Nova migration redirects, or merging product documentation.
- Executing activation before both the family copy and Eon site are accepted.

External contract:
- A visitor to `yazelix.com` can choose between Yazelix Nova and Yazelix Eon.
- `nova.yazelix.com` remains the stable Nova origin before and after family activation.
- `eon.yazelix.com` owns Eon.
- Neither product page describes the other as obsolete, legacy, or its release successor.

## Implementation Notes
- Keep the family landing page static and minimal.
- Prefer independent product deployments behind subdomains; share no documentation source of truth.
- Reuse visual brand assets directly where accepted, but do not create a shared theme package until repeated maintenance demonstrates a need.
- The Nova hosting decision only needs to permit independent future apex/Eon hosting; it does not need migration or redirect machinery.

## Verification
- The user explicitly activates this work after accepting the public Yazelix Eon site and family copy.
- DNS and valid TLS resolve for the apex, `nova`, and `eon` hosts.
- Nova routes and canonical URLs are identical before and after activation; no redirect loop or unintended recanonicalization is introduced.
- Apex and Eon canonical tags, sitemap entries, robots behavior, navigation, and social metadata name the correct host/product.
- Desktop/mobile and keyboard checks pass for the family landing page.
- Both product sites independently pass their release checks.

## Stop Conditions
- Stop while Yazelix Eon remains private, alpha-only, or lacks accepted public content.
- Stop if activation would require moving or recanonicalizing Nova.
- Do not make this bead a prerequisite for the Nova launch.
- Do not merge product documentation merely because the products share a brand.

## Maintenance
- Status: deferred until the trigger above.
- Effort: M.
- Risk: MEDIUM because apex/Eon DNS and public identity are user-facing, but Nova has no migration.
- Confidence: HIGH in the permanent Nova domain model; implementation timing depends on Yazelix Eon public readiness.
- Reconsideration trigger: an explicit user decision changing the Yazelix family/product naming or canonical domain strategy.

title: Choose one site-wide color-theme contract
description:
## Decision
Choose one coherent appearance contract before implementation:
1. Dark-only across custom pages and Starlight, removing the preference surface; or
2. Light/dark/auto across both shells, preserving choice across navigation and treating storage as optional.

## Evidence
- `src/styles/home.css:1-16` hard-codes custom pages dark.
- Starlight routes expose Light/Dark/Auto.
- Choosing Light on `/start/` then following All docs to `/docs/` returns to dark with no theme state/picker.
- If `localStorage` throws `SecurityError`, `src/components/ThemeProvider.astro:8-21` aborts; the picker can change while the document stays dark and client errors occur.
- Existing light and dark Starlight palettes pass contrast; this is contract ownership, not a palette request.

## Decision Scope
In: decide whether choice is public; name the theme owner; define first visit, cross-shell navigation, unavailable storage, system changes, and no-JS; record rejected option and smallest implementation boundary; create implementation work later if required.
Out: implementing either option here, new palettes, design-system rewrite, theme package, account sync, or Eon branding.

## Decision Criteria
Choose the fewest guarantees matching product intent. Accessibility requires coherence, not selectable light mode. If choice remains, storage failure must degrade safely.

## Verification
Record consumer/trigger/result/failure behavior, one owner, code/test boundary, and rejected alternative/rationale.

## Stop Conditions
Product-owner decision required because picker removal or cross-site light mode changes scope. Do not implement both options as compromise.

## Maintenance Notes
Effort: S. Downstream risk: MED. Accessibility impact: MED. Confidence: HIGH.
acceptance_criteria:
[ ] Owner selects dark-only or site-wide light/dark/auto.
[ ] Contract covers both shells, first visit, navigation, storage failure, system preference, and no JavaScript.
[ ] One owner and minimum implementation/test boundary are named.
[ ] Rejected alternative and rationale are recorded.
[ ] No implementation is mixed into this decision bead.

title: Emit stable combined Docs anchors in built HTML
description:
## Accepted Contract

Consumer: a visitor opening or sharing a fragment on combined `/docs/`.

Trigger: the static page is delivered, including before client scripts or with JavaScript disabled.

Observable result: every chapter and Markdown heading has one unique, chapter-prefixed ID in built HTML; every rail, heading-permalink, and same-document fragment points to an emitted target. Cold loads and browser history restore the intended heading. Standalone Starlight documents keep their original IDs and URLs.

Failure behavior: a missing ordered Docs entry fails the build. Client JavaScript enhances active-section state but neither creates nor rewrites anchor identity.

## Accepted Ownership

- `docsOrder` stores only the irreducible ordering of canonical content IDs.
- Astro native `getEntry` directly loads each ordered document; its entry ID owns the standalone URL and chapter identity, while its metadata owns the displayed title and description.
- `src/pages/docs/index.astro` computes each combined heading anchor once from the chapter anchor and Astro heading slug.
- The same heading record feeds both the rail and `src/components/PrefixedDocsContent.astro`.
- `PrefixedDocsContent.astro` renders the existing Starlight Markdown slot and substitutes supplied anchor identities at static-render time, preserving Starlight rendering and asset handling. Substitutions run longest source slug first so a generated prefixed value cannot be mistaken for a later source slug.
- The browser script reads emitted H2 IDs only; the post-load ID/permalink mutation path is deleted.
- Standalone Starlight rendering and public fragments remain unchanged.
- `ARCHITECTURE.md` records the build-time anchor owner.
- One no-JavaScript Playwright contract test covers uniqueness, all local fragments, cold navigation, back/forward restoration, and standalone compatibility.

No content, route, search, responsive-navigation, theme, dependency, provider, or standalone URL change is included.

## Verification

Proof applies to the task worktree based on `52cd009033e53b863575af81f5f67fa782949e7e`, Bun 1.3.13, Linux, 2026-08-09.

- TDD red before implementation: 46 IDs but only 43 unique IDs.
- Third-pass adversarial proof before the order fix: valid source slugs `foo` then `start-foo` collapsed to duplicate `start-start-foo` IDs and exited 1.
- The same adversarial proof after the order fix emits distinct `start-foo` and `start-start-foo` IDs and exits 0.
- `bun run check`: 16 files, zero errors, warnings, or hints.
- `bun run build`: 13 static pages; Pagefind indexed all 13.
- Built HTML: 46/46 unique IDs, all 83 same-page fragments and all 45 rail targets resolve.
- Simplification passes reduced runtime source by 16 lines from the initial green fix.
- The entire generated `dist/` tree is byte-for-byte identical across the accepted simplifications and edge-case fix.
- Full browser suite against built Astro preview: 34/34 passed across desktop Chromium and Pixel 7.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

## Maintenance Notes

The dedicated wrapper is the minimum platform-native boundary that can render and transform an Astro slot without bypassing Starlight or future asset handling. The ordered ID list intentionally contains no parallel labels or hrefs. The separate responsive/accessibility bead `yazelix-site-9vd` is unblocked.

title: Choose static hosting for the permanent Nova subdomain
description:
## Accepted Decision
GitHub Pages will permanently host Yazelix Nova at https://nova.yazelix.com. The public luccahuguet/yazelix-site repository and its GitHub Actions workflow own the deploy artifact. Hostinger remains the authoritative DNS provider; it does not own the site build or artifact.

## External Contract
A successful deployment publishes the exact static dist artifact built from one main commit at https://nova.yazelix.com. Failed builds do not replace the current deployment, and a known-good commit can be redeployed without changing the canonical host.

## Source and Trigger
- Source: the exact commit pushed to main in luccahuguet/yazelix-site.
- Trigger: push to main or an explicit workflow_dispatch run.
- Artifact owner: one bounded GitHub Actions workflow builds dist and deploys the GitHub Pages artifact.
- Jobs: a read-only build job followed by a dedicated deploy job using the github-pages environment.
- Limits: Linux only, no matrix, no pull-request preview, no schedule, no external cache service, ten-minute job timeouts, and Pages concurrency that prevents overlapping deploys.

## Permissions and Credentials
- Build job: contents: read.
- Deploy job: pages: write and id-token: write.
- Credentials: repository-provided GITHUB_TOKEN and OIDC only; no repository or provider secret is required.
- GitHub account luccahuguet has repository admin access and Actions is enabled.
- Lucca owns final cutover approval and the Hostinger DNS change.

## Domain, DNS, and TLS
1. Verify yazelix.com in the luccahuguet GitHub account with the GitHub-provided TXT record and retain that record to prevent Pages domain takeover.
2. Enable Pages with build_type workflow and successfully deploy the site artifact.
3. Bind nova.yazelix.com as the repository custom domain before publishing DNS.
4. In Hostinger DNS, add only CNAME nova -> luccahuguet.github.io. Do not include the repository path and do not add a wildcard.
5. Wait for GitHub DNS health and automatic Lets Encrypt certificate provisioning, then enforce HTTPS.
6. Confirm HTTP redirects to HTTPS and canonical output remains https://nova.yazelix.com.

The apex A record and both future Eon and apex deployment choices remain untouched. A later family site and eon.yazelix.com can use independent repositories or providers without moving Nova.

## 404 and Rollback
The existing generated dist/404.html is the custom GitHub Pages 404 surface. To restore a known-good deployment within GitHub Actions retention, rerun its successful workflow with gh run rerun RUN_ID; GitHub reruns with the same GITHUB_SHA and rebuilds that exact source. Beyond the rerun window, make an additive git revert on main and push it through the same workflow. Neither rollback changes DNS or the canonical host.

## Scope Held
This issue records the decision only. It does not enable Pages, add a workflow, change DNS, issue TLS, or publish the site.
design: GitHub Pages was selected because the source is already a public GitHub repository, the authenticated owner has admin access, Actions is enabled, Pages supports custom subdomains and managed HTTPS, and Astro documents a native Pages artifact path. Hostinger was rejected as artifact owner because current evidence confirms its DNS and parked apex but not an eligible web/cloud hosting plan; its Git integration would also add an OAuth deployment owner. Cloudflare Pages was rejected because it would require a new project/account integration while offering no needed capability beyond the same external-DNS CNAME model. The implementation should use explicit frozen Bun installation, diagnostics, and build steps rather than a provider abstraction. The platform custom-domain setting owns the hostname; a public/CNAME file is unnecessary for a custom Actions workflow. Official references: https://docs.astro.build/en/guides/deploy/github/, https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/using-custom-workflows-with-github-pages, https://docs.github.com/en/pages/configuring-a-custom-domain-for-your-github-pages-site/managing-a-custom-domain-for-your-github-pages-site, https://docs.github.com/en/pages/configuring-a-custom-domain-for-your-github-pages-site/verifying-your-custom-domain-for-github-pages, https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/securing-your-github-pages-site-with-https, https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/manage-workflow-runs/re-run-workflows-and-jobs, https://www.hostinger.com/support/1583302-how-to-deploy-a-git-repository-in-hostinger/, and https://developers.cloudflare.com/pages/configuration/custom-domains/.
acceptance_criteria:
Complete when:
- GitHub Pages is named as the artifact and publication owner.
- main push and manual dispatch are the only build triggers.
- Job boundaries, permissions, credentials, concurrency, and timeouts are explicit.
- The exact Hostinger CNAME, GitHub domain verification, custom-domain ordering, TLS owner, and HTTPS step are explicit.
- Existing dist/404.html behavior and exact-revision rollback are explicit.
- Lucca is the cutover authority.
- nova.yazelix.com remains permanent while apex and eon.yazelix.com remain independently deployable.
- No provider activation, workflow, DNS, or site implementation is included in this decision issue.
notes: Verified 2026-08-08: luccahuguet/yazelix-site is public with main as default; authenticated access has admin, push, and maintain permissions; Actions is enabled with a read-only default token; no Pages site or github-pages environment exists. Hostinger nameservers ns1.dns-parking.com and ns2.dns-parking.com are authoritative. The apex resolves to 2.57.91.91. nova.yazelix.com, eon.yazelix.com, the GitHub Pages verification TXT record, and apex CAA records do not exist. The repository has no deployment workflow or provider configuration, and astro.config.mjs already owns https://nova.yazelix.com.

title: Enforce canonical trailing-slash URLs on Vercel
description:
## Why
